result.note: Scope confirmed via git show --stat: only test/letflow/sandbox_pool_test.exs touched (+15/-0), purely additive after RT-9's existing final assertion, RT-2 and lib/letflow/sandbox_pool.ex untouched. Idiom correct: :DOWN tuple shape and pin-operator usage match this file's own established rendezvous idiom (RT-1..RT-8's assert_receive {:released,...}, pool_op_rendezvous_timeout() pattern); pool_op_rendezvous_timeout/0 confirmed to exist and evaluate to release_call_timeout() + slack = provision_timeout_ms() + slack, an appropriate bound. Race closure independently re-derived (not trusted from design/ELIXIR-DEV): state.in_flight.task_pid is literally the async_nolink Task's own pid; a monitor cannot deliver :DOWN before the monitored process actually terminates; ExUnit's LIFO on_exit ordering means blocking the test function's return until :DOWN fires guarantees all three on_exit callbacks (claimer kill guard, GenServer.stop, RT-9's own CASCADE drop) run strictly after the worker is confirmed dead. No quality regression from accepting any exit reason: the pool itself treats a crashed provisioning worker as an already-tested first-class outcome (classify_worker_result/2), RT-9's own documented purpose is the ISS-0227 key-set-shape regression already fully asserted before this step, binding _reason rather than :normal is correct and doesn't silently swallow anything. Independent verification: REVIEWER ran mix test test/letflow/sandbox_pool_test.exs 5 times with distinct seeds, 5/5 passed (23 passed each), corroborating ELIXIR-DEV's 24/24 and full test/letflow/ 3153/3153. mix compile --warnings-as-errors and mix format --check-formatted both clean.
